primary_direction.title: Ecological Cognitive Architecture Atlas
primary_direction.problem: Comparative demonstrations show striking but heterogeneous abilities, yet no validated framework separates shared flexibility from ecological expertise while controlling for sensory, motor, motivational, and training differences.
primary_direction.hypothesis: A partially shared latent flexibility factor will coexist with species-specific domain factors, and an affordance-aware mosaic model will predict held-out performance better than a universal intelligence factor.
primary_direction.novelty: ECAA measures generality through covariance and transfer while preserving species-specific ecological competence.
primary_direction.expected_result: Cross-domain covariance will be nonzero but incomplete; ecology and social learning will explain residual variance; domain rankings will reverse across species.
falsification: affordance terms add no explanatory value
social-learning manipulation has no downstream effect
single-factor model matches mosaic model on held-out tasks

portfolio.high_risk: phylogenetic Bayesian model of independent origins

search_trace.evidence: Emery et al. 2007; Seed et al. 2008

handoff_requirements: use affordance-matched common cores and species-specific modules
separate trained behavior from human-like concepts
